reasons: Rule expects a post-termination transition/data-return clause in a hosting agreement; the cited § 3.5 addresses only accrued payment obligations and the rationale accounts for the nearest candidates (§ 8.1 Materials return, § 14.18 contact-data processing, § 11.6 Content responsibility), none of which give Customer any exit or data-retrieval right — so 'missing' is the correct status and even the fallback (90 days' assistance, export within 30 days) is unmet.

Redline is actionable and minimal: it appends the model exit language (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return of Content, then deletion with written certification) to § 3.5 without disturbing existing text, and § 14.2 already lists § 3.5 as surviving, so the inserted obligation is enforceable post-termination.

Drafting is correctly party-mapped to IBM as the performing party and to 'Content' as the operative data term; the 'within thirty (30) days of Customer's request' tweak is a harmless variant of the model language.
Comment is concise, first person plural, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback; deterministic checks pass.
